analysis: Both primary units are base_text excerpts of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 547-1286). This is a docs-only change. The patch excerpt (truncated) shows a date bump, plus new prose in the load_model, prefetch_model and desired-models sections. The prose says a provider without Autopilot refuses models outside an operator filter with `model_not_selected` (`autopilotAllowsModel`), and that prefetch_model is refused before any download. These additions describe provider-side restriction. They do not add wire fields, relax authentication, or change attestation, encryption or the cache. They stay within the existing TB-002 coordinator-to-provider contract and the A-004 model-weights concerns. Nothing in the visible changes weakens the T-041 prefix-cache posture, TB-011 authorization, T-053 binding, or the encrypted request path. The base excerpts I examined include the models_replace validation and drain fence, cache receipt v2 rules, capacity telemetry, inference_error sanitization, and attestation_response. All of that is unchanged by the visible patch. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated at the desired-models paragraph, which is the last visible hunk. Head-side text for the new operator-filter behavior was not supplied. The referenced configuration.md anchor and the Swift `autopilotAllowsModel` implementation are not in evidence. So I cannot confirm that the documented refusal matches code. A documentation mismatch would be a drift risk, not a verified regression. No concrete security regression is identified. A reviewer of the source change should check that the filter is enforced before any download or load, and that it cannot be bypassed via Autopilot or desired_models paths.
